name: Tools System Design for codx-junior
description:
## Summary

1. **Tools System Design** for codx-junior enables reusable, executable scripts run inside isolated Docker containers, scoped either globally or per-project.
2. **Tool Definitions** are JSON files describing the script, Docker image, inputs (including secret types), roles, and output format, stored on the filesystem mirroring the existing profiles pattern.
3. **Execution Model** spawns ephemeral Docker containers per invocation, passing inputs as `INPUT_*` environment variables to prevent injection, capturing stdout/stderr and returning structured JSON results.
4. **Security** enforces role-based access (admin creates/edits, developers execute if permitted), masks secrets in all logs and records, and runs containers without elevated privileges.
5. **Delivery** is planned in 5 phases: from tool definition & CRUD API → Docker execution → project-scoped tools → role-based access → execution history & analytics.

We must be able to define a set of tools (scripts) that will be able to be executed in a project (and related projects) in a docker container.
Example of a tool will be "Load Azure Pull Request"


The load_azure_pull_request will receive Azure CLI PAT or other requiered user settings to connect with azure and a pull request url, when executed it will return the pull request info in JSON.


Execution must be in docker container, docker engine is already in place and accessible through commands or a python lib if any exists.


Tools will be global or project specific, storing the tool definition in the project .codx/tools folder or using a global folder for it.


Only admins can create tools.
Added files for rteferences.

Create a document with the design of the new tools functionality, no coding yet just analysis and discussion.

# codx-junior Tools System — Design Document

## 1. Overview

This document describes the design for a **Tools System** within codx-junior. Tools are reusable, executable scripts that run inside isolated Docker containers. They can be scoped globally or to a specific project and are invocable from any project that has access to them.

The motivating example is `load_azure_pull_request` — a tool that, given an Azure DevOps PAT and a pull request URL, fetches and returns the PR details as JSON.

---

## 2. Goals

- Allow admins to define scripts (tools) that can be executed on demand.
- Execute tools safely in isolated Docker containers.
- Support **global tools** (available to all projects) and **project-specific tools**.
- Tool definitions are stored on the filesystem alongside project configuration.
- Tools can accept user-supplied parameters at execution time.
- Tool results are returned as structured JSON.
- Non-admin users can **execute** tools they have access to but cannot create or modify them.

---

## 3. Non-Goals (v1)

- Tool versioning / rollback.
- A visual tool builder UI (CLI/API only for now).
- Tool execution scheduling / cron triggers.
- Streaming output from long-running tools (may be added later).

---

## 4. Concepts & Terminology

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Tool** | A named, versioned script with declared inputs and a Docker execution context. |
| **Tool Definition** | The JSON/YAML file that describes the tool (name, script, image, inputs, scope). |
| **Tool Execution** | A single invocation of a tool with a specific set of argument values. |
| **Tool Result** | The JSON output produced by a tool execution. |
| **Global Tool** | A tool stored in a global folder, available to every project. |
| **Project Tool** | A tool stored inside `.codx/tools/` of a specific project. |
| **Tool Scope** | Combination of global and all project tools visible to a given execution context. |

---

## 5. Tool Definition Schema

Each tool is described by a JSON file. Below is the proposed schema with commentary.

```json
{
  "id": "load_azure_pull_request",
  "name": "Load Azure Pull Request",
  "description": "Fetches pull request details from Azure DevOps and returns them as JSON.",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scope": "global",
  "docker": {
    "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/azure-cli:latest",
    "working_dir": "/workspace",
    "network": "host",
    "timeout_seconds": 60,
    "environment": {}
  },
  "inputs": [
    {
      "name": "pat",
      "label": "Azure PAT Token",
      "type": "secret",
      "required": true,
      "description": "Personal Access Token for Azure DevOps authentication."
    },
    {
      "name": "pull_request_url",
      "label": "Pull Request URL",
      "type": "string",
      "required": true,
      "description": "Full URL of the Azure DevOps pull request."
    },
    {
      "name": "organization",
      "label": "Azure Organization",
      "type": "string",
      "required": false,
      "description": "Azure DevOps organization name (inferred from URL if omitted)."
    }
  ],
  "script": "az devops configure --defaults organization=https://dev.azure.com/$(organization)\naz repos pr show --id $(pull_request_id) --output json",
  "output_format": "json",
  "roles": ["admin", "developer"],
  "tags": ["azure", "git", "pr"]
}
```

### Field Notes

- **`id`** — Unique machine-readable identifier (snake_case). Used in API paths.
- **`scope`** — `"global"` or `"project"`. Determines storage location.
- **`docker.image`** — The container image to spin up for execution.
- **`docker.timeout_seconds`** — Hard kill after this many seconds.
- **`inputs[].type`** — One of: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `secret`, `text`. `secret` values are masked in logs.
- **`script`** — The bash/shell script body. Input values are interpolated using `$(variable_name)` syntax.
- **`output_format`** — `json` or `text`. When `json`, the last line (or full stdout) is parsed and returned.
- **`roles`** — Which user roles can execute this tool. Admins always have access.

---

## 6. Storage Layout

### 6.1 Global Tools

```
/home/codx-junior/tools/
  load_azure_pull_request.tool.json
  another_global_tool.tool.json
```

The global tools path is configurable via an environment variable:

```
CODX_JUNIOR_TOOLS_PATH=/home/codx-junior/tools
```

### 6.2 Project-Specific Tools

```
/home/codx-junior-projects/my-project/.codx/tools/
  my_custom_tool.tool.json
  another_project_tool.tool.json
```

This mirrors how profiles are stored in `.codx/profiles/`.

### 6.3 Tool Discovery Order

When resolving tools for a project the system merges tools from multiple sources. Later sources override earlier ones when IDs collide:

```
Global tools  →  Parent project tools  →  Current project tools
```

This mirrors `ProfileManager.list_all_profiles()` logic already in the codebase.

---

## 7. Execution Model

### 7.1 Isolation via Docker

Each tool execution spawns a **fresh, ephemeral Docker container**:

```
docker run --rm \
  --network host \
  --timeout N \
  -e INPUT_PAT="..." \
  -e INPUT_PULL_REQUEST_URL="..." \
  -v /tmp/codx-tool-workspace-<uuid>:/workspace \
  <image> \
  bash -c "<script body>"
```

Key properties:
- `--rm` — Container is deleted immediately after completion.
- A unique temporary directory is mounted as `/workspace` to give the script a clean writable area.
- All inputs are passed as environment variables prefixed with `INPUT_` to avoid shell injection risks.
- `secret` type inputs are passed the same way but **never logged**.

### 7.2 Script Variable Interpolation

The `$(variable_name)` placeholders in the script body are **replaced server-side before execution** with `$INPUT_VARIABLE_NAME` references, keeping actual secret values out of the command line and inside environment variables:

```bash
# Tool script (stored):
az repos pr show --id $(pull_request_url) --org https://dev.azure.com/ --token $(pat)

# Rendered for docker run:
az repos pr show --id "$INPUT_PULL_REQUEST_URL" --org https://dev.azure.com/ --token "$INPUT_PAT"
```

### 7.3 Output Collection

- **stdout** is captured as the tool result.
- **stderr** is captured separately and included in the execution record for diagnostics.
- When `output_format == "json"`, stdout is parsed. If parsing fails, an error is returned.
- Exit code `0` = success; anything else = failure.

### 7.4 Execution Record

Every execution produces an `ToolExecution` record:

```json
{
  "execution_id": "<uuid>",
  "tool_id": "load_azure_pull_request",
  "project_id": "abc-123",
  "triggered_by": "admin_user",
  "started_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "finished_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:05Z",
  "status": "success",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "stdout": "{ ... }",
  "stderr": "",
  "result": { ... }
}
```

Execution records are stored in:
```
/home/codx-junior/analytics/tool_executions/<tool_id>/<execution_id>.json
```

---

## 8. Security Model

### 8.1 Who Can Do What

| Action | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create/Edit/Delete global tool | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Create/Edit/Delete project tool | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| List available tools | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Execute a tool | ✅ | if in `roles` | ❌ |
| View execution history | ✅ | own only | ❌ |

### 8.2 Secret Handling

- `secret` inputs are **never written to disk** (not in the tool definition, not in execution records).
- They are passed only as ephemeral Docker environment variables.
- They are masked as `***` in any log entries.
- The API response for execution records will omit secret values.

### 8.3 Docker Security Considerations

- Containers run with minimal privileges (no `--privileged` flag unless explicitly declared).
- Network access is `host` by default but configurable per tool.
- Image must be explicitly declared — no dynamic image selection from user input.
- The temporary `/workspace` volume is cleaned up after execution.

---

## 9. API Surface

All tool endpoints live under `/api/tools`.

### Admin Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/tools` | List all tools (global + project-scoped) |
| `POST` | `/api/tools` | Create a new global tool |
| `PUT` | `/api/tools/{tool_id}` | Update a global tool |
| `DELETE` | `/api/tools/{tool_id}` | Delete a global tool |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools` | List tools for a project |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools` | Create a project-specific tool |
| `PUT` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools/{tool_id}` | Update a project tool |
| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools/{tool_id}` | Delete a project tool |

### User Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools/accessible` | List tools the user can execute |
| `POST` | `/api/tools/{tool_id}/execute` | Execute a global tool |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{project_id}/tools/{tool_id}/execute` | Execute a project tool |
| `GET` | `/api/tools/executions/{execution_id}` | Get a single execution result |
| `GET` | `/api/tools/{tool_id}/executions` | List executions for a tool |

---

## 10. Data Models (Conceptual)

```
ToolInput
  name: str
  label: str
  type: Literal["string", "number", "boolean", "secret", "text"]
  required: bool
  description: str
  default_value: Optional[str]

ToolDockerSettings
  image: str
  working_dir: str = "/workspace"
  network: str = "host"
  timeout_seconds: int = 60
  environment: dict = {}

Tool
  id: str
  name: str
  description: str
  version: str
  scope: Literal["global", "project"]
  project_id: Optional[str]          # set when scope == "project"
  docker: ToolDockerSettings
  inputs: List[ToolInput]
  script: str
  output_format: Literal["json", "text"] = "json"
  roles: List[str] = []
  tags: List[str] = []
  created_by: str
  updated_at: str

ToolExecutionRequest
  inputs: dict                        # key=input.name, value=supplied value

ToolExecution
  execution_id: str
  tool_id: str
  project_id: Optional[str]
  triggered_by: str
  started_at: str
  finished_at: Optional[str]
  status: Literal["pending", "running", "success", "failed", "timeout"]
  exit_code: Optional[int]
  stdout: Optional[str]
  stderr: Optional[str]
  result: Optional[dict]              # parsed when output_format == "json"
```

---

## 11. ToolManager Class (Conceptual)

Mirrors `ProfileManager` in structure:

```
ToolManager(settings: CODXJuniorSettings)
  ├── list_global_tools() → List[Tool]
  ├── list_project_tools() → List[Tool]
  ├── list_all_tools() → List[Tool]          # merged, project overrides global
  ├── get_tool(tool_id) → Tool
  ├── save_tool(tool: Tool)
  ├── delete_tool(tool_id)
  └── execute_tool(tool, inputs, user) → ToolExecution
```

`execute_tool` delegates to a `DockerToolRunner`:

```
DockerToolRunner
  ├── prepare_environment(tool, inputs) → dict[str, str]
  ├── render_script(tool, inputs) → str
  ├── run(tool, env, script) → (stdout, stderr, exit_code)
  └── cleanup(workspace_path)
```

---

## 12. Integration Points with Existing Codebase

| Existing Component | Integration Point |
|---|---|
| `CODXJuniorSettings` | `get_tools_path()` method, analogous to `get_profiles_path()` |
| `ProfileManager` | `ToolManager` mirrors its discovery and storage pattern |
| `project_discover.py` | `find_project_by_id` used to resolve project context for execution |
| `GlobalSettings` | Add a `tools_path` field; global tools stored there |
| `globals.py` | Add `CODX_JUNIOR_TOOLS_PATH` constant |
| `require_admin` / `get_authenticated_user` | Reused as-is for tool endpoint auth |
| `workspaces.py` / `_user_has_workspace_access` | Role check pattern reused for `roles` field on tools |
| Analytics path (`ANALYTICS_DATA_PATH`) | Execution records stored under existing analytics folder |

---

## 13. Example: `load_azure_pull_request` End-to-End

```
1. Admin POSTs to /api/tools with the tool definition JSON.
   → Saved to /home/codx-junior/tools/load_azure_pull_request.tool.json

2. Developer GETs /api/projects/my-project/tools/accessible
   → Tool appears if "developer" is in tool.roles

3. Developer POSTs to /api/projects/my-project/tools/load_azure_pull_request/execute
   Body: { "inputs": { "pat": "xxxx", "pull_request_url": "https://..." } }

4. Server validates all required inputs are present.

5. DockerToolRunner:
   a. Creates temp dir /tmp/codx-tool-workspace-<uuid>
   b. Builds env: { "INPUT_PAT": "xxxx", "INPUT_PULL_REQUEST_URL": "https://..." }
   c. Renders script (variable refs → $INPUT_* env vars)
   d. Runs: docker run --rm -e INPUT_PAT=xxxx ... mcr.microsoft.com/azure-cli bash -c "..."
   e. Captures stdout/stderr

6. Output (stdout JSON) is parsed and returned:
   {
     "execution_id": "...",
     "status": "success",
     "result": { "pullRequestId": 42, "title": "...", ... }
   }

7. Execution record saved to analytics (with PAT masked).
```

---

## 14. Open Questions

1. **Should tools support streaming output?** Useful for long-running tools but adds complexity. Defer to v2.
2. **Image pre-pulling strategy** — Should the system pre-pull Docker images declared in tool definitions to avoid cold-start latency? Or pull lazily on first use?
3. **Input value persistence** — Should non-secret input values be saved per-user as defaults for convenience? Needs UX discussion.
4. **Tool execution quotas** — Should there be rate limiting per user/tool to prevent runaway executions?
5. **Audit trail retention** — How long should execution records be kept? Should they be pruned automatically?
6. **Tool import/export** — Should tools be shareable as portable JSON bundles?
7. **Mounted project files** — Should the current project path be mounted into the container automatically so tools can read/write project files?

---

## 15. Phased Delivery

| Phase | Scope |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | Tool definition model, `ToolManager`, global tool CRUD API (admin only), filesystem storage |
| **Phase 2** | `DockerToolRunner`, execute endpoint, basic execution records |
| **Phase 3** | Project-scoped tools, tool discovery/merging across project hierarchy |
| **Phase 4** | Role-based execution access, accessible tools endpoint for users |
| **Phase 5** | Execution history API, analytics integration, secret masking in logs |
